page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmsv2 family. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for integer and tile operations. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

This server is heavily memory-optimized, providing 1344.0 GB of RAM, which translates to an exceptionally high ratio of 84.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include any local storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on external Premium Storage options. There are no GPUs bundled with this instance, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the FX64-16ms_v2 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring 2364.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and showing strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.83 GB/sec. Large-block memory write bandwidth is strong at 91.25 GB/sec, while multi-core performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations perform in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the complete lack of local storage and the high memory-to-vCPU ratio, which makes it highly specialized. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory capacity per compute unit without needing local disk I/O. Best-fit workloads include memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from high clock speeds and large memory footprints.
